notes.summary: Full-family continuity for every finite continuous obstacle on explicit compact strict rational curve affinoids over an algebraically closed nontrivially valued field. Global LFS realization, comparison and compatibility with every analytic scalar extension are proved. This is a sufficient sector, not the sharp classification.
notes.detailedSummary: Finite type-2 trees uniformly approximate arbitrary continuous obstacles on the displayed rational domains. A greatest admissible vertex vector is globally realized by truncated logarithms with nonnegative interior charges and signed boundary-unit logarithms. Rational-star, annulus and omitted-disc comparisons bound every competitor in the exact union. Translation contractivity proves continuity for arbitrary obstacles and supplies uniform approximation by global LFS minorants. Passing arbitrary scalar extensions through their completed algebraic closures proves exact envelope pullback without assuming scalar projection is open. General semistable affinoids, arbitrary ground fields and the original sharp classification remain unresolved.
notes.text:
This is a partial mathematical theorem concerning the full competitor union.

Let \(K\) be complete, algebraically closed and nontrivially valued. Choose centres \(a_0,\ldots,a_m\in K\) and radii \(R,r_i\in|K^\times|\) satisfying
\[
0<r_i<R,\qquad |a_i-a_0|<R,\qquad |a_i-a_j|>\max(r_i,r_j)\quad(i\ne j).
\]
Define the actual compact strict rational affinoid
\[
D=\{|T-a_0|\le R\}\setminus\bigcup_i\{|T-a_i|<r_i\}.
\]
The case \(m=0\) is a closed strict disc. For every finite continuous \(f\) on \(D\), the raw envelope \(E_Df\) over all globally defined locally Fubini–Study or semipositive real-PL minorants is finite and continuous. Consequently \((E_Df)^*=E_Df\). Moreover, for every analytic extension \(F/K\),
\[
E_{D_F}(f\circ\pi)=E_Df\circ\pi.
\]
The upstairs envelope is also continuous. No invariance condition is imposed on \(f\) or on competitors.

Checked published foundations. Gubler–Jell–Rabinoff, cached arXiv:2111.05741, Definition 5.1 and Lemma 5.4, define real PL using strict G-local linear combinations of logarithms of analytic units and give continuity and pullback. Definition 7.8 defines LFS as an R-PL function with semiample residue at every point, hence semipositive. Paragraph 7.9 gives the precise ordinary-local presentation
\[
h=\sum_j\lambda_j\max_i\{-\log|u_{ji}|\},\qquad \lambda_j\ge0,\quad u_{ji}\in\mathcal O^\times.
\]
The minus signs and invertibility requirement were checked against original PDF page 47. Proposition 7.6 preserves semipositivity under analytic morphisms and every analytic field extension. Gubler–Rabinoff, arXiv:2506.13548v2, Theorem 4.3, identifies semipositive real PL with classical psh on good strict spaces over a nontrivially valued field, without a boundaryless hypothesis. Its Definitions 3.4 and 4.1 quantify over all analytic extensions and curve morphisms. Theorems 6.1 and 6.4 provide the interior local maximum principle and affinoid Shilov maximum principle. These foundations apply to every competitor here. Arbitrary maxima of real-PL functions are not assumed real PL; GJR Example 5.3 expressly warns against that assertion.

Boundary verification. Put \(o=\xi_{a_0,R}\), \(b_i=\xi_{a_i,r_i}\), and \(B=\{o,b_i\}\). The nested-disc topology described in GR2 Appendix A shows that the ordinary boundary of \(D\) in the boundaryless projective line is exactly \(B\). The analytic-domain interior formula in GR2 Section 2.11 identifies this with the analytic boundary. The domain is connected by its disc tree. A continuous psh function has its maximum on \(B\): otherwise its nonempty closed maximum locus is contained in the interior and is open by the local maximum principle, contradicting connectedness. The same reasoning applies to the finite maximum locus of \(\log|G|\) for nonzero analytic \(G\). Thus \(B\) is a boundary for analytic functions. It is the Shilov boundary: \((T-a_0)/c_0\), with \(|c_0|=R\), uniquely peaks at \(o\) among \(B\), whereas \(c_i/(T-a_i)\), with \(|c_i|=r_i\), uniquely peaks at \(b_i\). The imposed strict inequalities make all the other listed values smaller. This verification also applies to the smaller rational stars, discs and annuli below.

Actual finite trees and density. Take the finite hull \(\Gamma\subset D\) of \(B\) and finitely many additional type-2 points, including all branch points as vertices. Root it at \(o\), and use length \(|d\log r|\) along radius paths. Branch points have radii equal to centre distances and are type 2. For a nonroot vertex \(v=\xi_{a_v,r_v}\), define
\[
k_v(x)=\log\max\{|T-a_v|(x),r_v\}-\log R
=-\operatorname{length}([o,x]\cap[o,v]).
\]
The equality follows because the least common containing disc has radius \(\max(|T-a_v|(x),r_v)\); it persists for nested-disc limits, including type-4 points. The last point of \([o,x]\) in \(\Gamma\) defines \(\tau_\Gamma(x)\). The finitely many coordinates \(k_v\) separate points of \(\Gamma\) and have the same values at \(x\) and \(\tau_\Gamma(x)\). Their continuous embedding of compact \(\Gamma\) has continuous inverse, proving continuity of this actual retraction. Every component off \(\Gamma\) is an attached open disc; original holes are recorded in \(B\). Such a component is exhausted by smaller closed strict discs, whose Gauss points approach its attachment. Its closure is not silently assumed affinoid.

The finite continuous functions \(u_{a,r}=\log\max(|T-a|,r)\), for \(a\in K\) and \(r\in|K^\times|\), together with constants separate points of \(D\). Indeed seminorms are determined by polynomials, and algebraic closedness factors every polynomial into linear terms. A sufficiently small value-group truncation preserves a differing linear-factor value. Real Stone–Weierstrass therefore makes their generated algebra uniformly dense in \(C(D,\mathbb R)\). Each expression involving finitely many coordinates factors through a finite tree: endpoints outside \(D\) are truncated at the relevant boundary, and coordinates from centres outside the outer disc are constant. A continuous function on this finite tree can be uniformly approximated by edge-affine interpolation. Subdivision points can be type 2, since the nonzero divisible group \(\log|K^\times|\) is dense in \(\mathbb R\). Hence every continuous obstacle has uniform approximants
\[
F=\varphi\circ\tau_\Gamma,
\]
where \(\varphi\) is affine on each subdivided edge. This proves density in the actual analytic category.

Finite graph envelope and global realization. Write \(\ell_{vw}>0\) for edge lengths. Consider all vertex vectors satisfying
\[
q_v\le\varphi(v),\qquad
\sum_{w\sim v}\frac{q_w-q_v}{\ell_{vw}}\ge0\quad(v\notin B).
\]
Boundary vertices have no charge sign condition. Constants below \(\min\varphi\) are admissible. Coordinatewise maxima of admissible vectors remain admissible: choose the vector attaining the maximum at the tested vertex, and all neighbouring maxima are at least its neighbouring values. This is a finite-vector operation, not analytic maximum closure. The coordinatewise supremum \(p\) is finite, and taking finite maxima of almost maximizing vectors followed by a limit proves that \(p\) itself is admissible and greatest.

Let \(P\) interpolate \(p\) linearly and set
\[
d_v=\sum_{w\sim v}\frac{p_w-p_v}{\ell_{vw}},\qquad
Q=p_o+\sum_{v\ne o}d_vk_v.
\]
The outgoing charge of \(k_v\) is \(+1\) at \(v\), \(-1\) at \(o\), and zero elsewhere. Consequently \(Q=P\circ\tau_\Gamma\): subtract the two expressions on the tree and remove terminal vertices successively; the difference has zero slope on each removed edge and is zero at the root.

This is an actual global LFS minorant. At an interior vertex \(d_v\ge0\). A truncated logarithm is strict PL on the two strict domains \(|T-a_v|\le r_v\) and \(|T-a_v|\ge r_v\); on the latter \(T-a_v\) is a unit. At a bend, choose an ordinary neighbourhood excluding its zero and use
\[
\log\max(|T-a_v|,r_v)
=\max\{-\log|(T-a_v)^{-1}|,-\log|c_v^{-1}|\},\quad |c_v|=r_v.
\]
Near its centre it is constant. These verify the exact LFS presentation. For \(v=b_i\), the coordinate equals \(\log|T-a_i|-\log R\) on all of \(D\), a logarithm of a global unit plus a constant. Its coefficient can have either sign, using an inverse unit for a negative coefficient. Real constants are LFS because the valuation is nontrivial. Thus positive interior terms and signed harmonic boundary terms give a global LFS function. The vertex obstacle inequalities imply \(P\le\varphi\) on every edge, hence \(Q\le F\).

Full-family upper bound. Let \(h\) be any competitor for \(F\). It is finite continuous and classically psh. At an interior vertex choose type-2 endpoints inside the adjacent edges, approaching the neighbouring vertices. The intervening rational star is a closed disc minus the open child discs, contained in the interior of \(D\); original holes lie beyond its endpoints. Let parent distance and value be \(L_+,t_+\), and child distances and values \(L_j,t_j\). Define
\[
M=\frac{t_+/L_++\sum_jt_j/L_j}{1/L_++\sum_j1/L_j}.
\]
On the star the child-centre functions \(T-a_j\) are units. The harmonic function
\[
H=C+\sum_j\frac{M-t_j}{L_j}\log|T-a_j|,\qquad H(v)=M,
\]
has exactly the specified endpoint values: the corresponding child logarithm decreases by \(L_j\) towards its child, and all child logarithms increase by \(L_+\) towards the parent. If there are no children, use the constant \(t_+\). Since \(h-H\) is psh, boundary comparison gives \(h(v)\le M\). Let endpoints tend to neighbours, using continuity of this competitor. Its vertex values satisfy the displayed graph inequalities, and hence \(h(v)\le p_v\).

On an open edge use smaller closed strict annuli with endpoints inside that edge and approaching its vertices. These avoid sibling holes at either vertex. Harmonic interpolation in log radius bounds \(h\) by interpolation of its endpoint values, hence by \(P\). At any omitted-disc point, the singleton-Shilov maximum principle on smaller closed discs bounds \(h\) by its value at their Gauss points; their limit is the attachment. Therefore \(h\le P\circ\tau_\Gamma=Q\) everywhere. Combined with the constructed global minorant,
\[
E_DF=Q.
\]
Every competitor in the exact full union has been bounded. Equality also holds for the LFS branch alone.

Passage to arbitrary continuous obstacles. Constant minorants exist by compactness. Both branches allow real constant translation, so the full-family envelope is monotone, translation equivariant and satisfies
\[
\|E_Yf-E_Yf'\|_\infty\le\|f-f'\|_\infty.
\]
Choose the finite-tree approximants \(F_n\) with errors \(\varepsilon_n\to0\). Their envelopes \(Q_n\) are continuous and converge uniformly to \(E_Df\), proving continuity. Moreover \(Q_n-\varepsilon_n\) are global LFS minorants of \(f\) and converge uniformly to the same envelope. No monotonicity or unjustified real-PL maximum closure is required.

All scalar extensions. For arbitrary \(F'/K\), pass to its completed algebraic closure \(L\). The finite hull of the same Gauss endpoints in \(D_L\) has identical lengths, branching and charges; these are computed from unchanged centres, distances and radii. The coordinate formulas identify the pulled obstacle with \(\varphi\circ\tau_{\Gamma_L}\) and the pulled \(Q\) with \(P\circ\tau_{\Gamma_L}\). New residual directions are included in the omitted-disc comparison. Every competitor on \(D_{F'}\) pulls back to a semipositive real-PL competitor on \(D_L\), where the entire-family computation bounds it by the pulled \(Q\). Surjectivity of scalar projection, GR2 Section 2.9, brings this bound down to \(D_{F'}\). Conversely the pulled \(Q\) is LFS by its explicit presentation. Thus exact pullback holds for finite-tree obstacles. Uniform approximation and envelope contractivity prove the asserted equality for every \(f\). Both envelopes are already continuous; scalar openness is unnecessary. This concerns base obstacles and their pullbacks, not unrelated arbitrary obstacles over every nonalgebraically closed extension.

Curve tests and scope. After every analytic extension, pull the uniform LFS minorants back to any smooth strict curve. They are subharmonic. On a strict affinoid in that curve, a harmonic function dominating the limit on the finite boundary dominates each approximant up to its uniform error; comparison and passage to the limit prove the curve test. GR2 Definitions 3.4 and 4.1 then supply the full curve quantifiers, including further extensions. Classical positivity is thus checked separately from continuity; no CLD-v2 conclusion is asserted. The sharp geometric classification, general semistable affinoids and unrestricted higher dimensions are not proved.

notes.summary: The full competitor envelope on a compact strict analytic base times projective space reduces exactly to the base envelope of the fibre-minimum obstacle. Combined with n1, this proves full-family continuity on the displayed rational-curve/projective-space products, with arbitrary obstacles and every scalar extension.
notes.detailedSummary: Scalar-stable positivity and the maximum principle make every competitor constant on each actual proper projective fibre over a completed residue field. An analytic section descends competitors, and analytic pullback supplies the converse. Proper closedness and relative-smooth openness prove continuity of the fibre minimum. Scalar projections between projective fibres are surjective, preserving that minimum. The reduction covers projective-space factors and handles the total space's relative boundary; it does not cover closed-polydisc products or establish the general higher-dimensional classification.
notes.text:
Let \(A\) be any compact good separated strictly \(K\)-analytic space over a complete nontrivially valued field. Put
\[
Z=A\times_K\mathbb P^{d,\mathrm{an}}_K,\qquad p:Z\to A,
\qquad s(x)=(x,[1:0:\cdots:0]).
\]
For every finite continuous obstacle \(f\), define
\[
g(x)=\min_{z\in p^{-1}(x)}f(z).
\]
Then \(g\) is finite continuous and the exact full-union raw envelopes satisfy
\[
E_Zf=(E_Ag)\circ p.
\]
For the rational domains \(A=D\) of n1, this proves continuity of the raw and regularized envelope on every \(D\times\mathbb P^{d,\mathrm{an}}\), for every arbitrary continuous obstacle. Exact compatibility with every analytic scalar extension also follows.

Proof of the actual proper-fibre mechanism. At every Berkovich point \(x\), the fibre is \(\mathbb P^{d,\mathrm{an}}_{\mathcal H(x)}\), not an assumed topological product fibre. Projective analytification is proper by Berkovich 1993, Proposition 2.6.9; analytic base change preserves properness. Each fibre is compact, good, strict over \(\mathcal H(x)\), and boundaryless.

It is connected over any complete field \(H\). On a closed polydisc of radius \(S\), take the Gauss norm of \(G(T(z)+W)\) in \(W\) with radius \(t\in[0,S]\). On polynomials this gives
\[
|G|_{z,t}=\max_\alpha |(\partial^{[\alpha]}G)(z)|t^{|\alpha|}.
\]
These multiplicative seminorms depend continuously on \((z,t)\), equal \(z\) at zero, and equal the radius-\(S\) Gauss point at \(S\), since bounded translation preserves that Gauss norm. Thus polydiscs are connected and their increasing union, affine analytic space, is connected. Its projective affine chart is dense: at a point on the omitted hyperplane, the same small Gauss deformation in the coordinate defining that hyperplane produces nonzero coordinate norm for every positive \(t\) and approaches the original point. Projective analytic space is therefore connected.

Take any competitor \(h\) on \(Z\). Scalar extension followed by analytic pullback restricts it to a semipositive real-PL, hence classically psh, function on the actual fibre. It attains a maximum by compactness. The maximum locus is nonempty and closed, and it is open by the interior local maximum principle because the fibre has no boundary. Connectedness forces \(h\) constant on that fibre. Therefore \(h=a\circ p\), where \(a=h\circ s\).

Analytic restriction along \(s\) preserves real PL and semipositivity by the checked GJR pullback theorems. If \(h\) is LFS, its ordinary-local unit-max presentation restricts along \(s\), so \(a\) is also LFS. Conversely pullback along \(p\) preserves both branches. This proves an exact family bijection. The inequality \(a\circ p\le f\) is equivalent to \(a\le g\), establishing the raw-envelope identity for the entire union.

The fibre minimum is continuous. The proper projection is topologically closed. It is relatively smooth: on projective coordinate charts it is \(\mathbb A^d_A\to A\), the local form of Berkovich Definition 3.5.1. Corollary 3.7.4, checked in the original PDF, makes it topologically open. For every real \(t\),
\[
\{g\le t\}=p(\{f\le t\})\text{ is closed},\qquad
\{g<t\}=p(\{f<t\})\text{ is open}.
\]
Thus \(g\) is continuous. Applying n1 proves continuity and uniform global LFS approximation on the displayed products. The absolute analytic boundary is \(p^{-1}(B)\), by the relative-interior composition formula and relative boundarylessness of \(p\). The maximum principle above was applied on the fibre, not on the boundaryful total space.

For every analytic extension \(F/K\), the fibre over \(x'\in A_F\) maps surjectively to the fibre over \(x=\pi(x')\). This is the scalar projection from projective space over \(\mathcal H(x')\) to projective space over \(\mathcal H(x)\). Hence the fibre minimum of \(f\circ\pi_Z\) is exactly \(g\circ\pi_A\). Apply the same full-family reduction over \(F\), followed by n1's scalar identity for \(g\), to obtain
\[
E_{Z_F}(f\circ\pi_Z)=E_Zf\circ\pi_Z
\]
when \(A=D\). The uniform approximants also pass every extended analytic-curve test as proved in n1.

Finally any continuous open surjection satisfies \((a\circ p)^*=a^*\circ p\) for locally bounded \(a\). Continuity gives the inequality \(\le\) using pulled-back neighbourhoods; openness gives \(\ge\) because the image of every neighbourhood of a lift is a neighbourhood of its image. Thus the reduction also describes regularization over a base with a discontinuous raw envelope.

notes.summary: A fresh exact full-family split-node calculation gives a discontinuous regularized envelope for a finite continuous obstacle. The obstruction persists under scalar extension and projective-space products. This supplies a concrete necessary exclusion, not the original sharp classification.
notes.detailedSummary: On the split nodal affinoid, take zero obstacle on the x-disc and minus a times the y-coordinate norm on the y-disc. Every competitor is bounded by minus a throughout the y-disc by analytic branch pullback and its singleton-Shilov maximum principle. Explicit global LFS truncated logarithms approach zero at every nonnodal x-point. The raw envelope is exactly zero on the punctured x-branch and minus a on the y-branch including the node. Regularization raises the node to zero and is discontinuous along the other branch. The proper-fibre reduction and smooth openness carry this failure to every projective-space product. General necessity and unrestricted continuity remain unproved; candidate is false.
notes.text:
This counterexample is proved independently; no supplied book claim is assumed.

Over any complete nontrivially valued field let
\[
U=\mathcal M(K\langle x,y\rangle/(xy)).
\]
Its two closed strict branch discs \(D_x,D_y\) meet at their common rigid origin \(n\). For \(a>0\), define
\[
f|_{D_x}=0,\qquad f|_{D_y}=-a|y|.
\]
This is finite continuous: it is also the global function \(-a|y|\), and the two branch restrictions agree at the node.

For any competitor in the exact full union, analytic restriction to \(D_y\) preserves semipositivity and classical pshness by the published foundations checked in n1. Its singleton Shilov boundary is the radius-one Gauss point \(\eta_y\). Therefore
\[
h|_{D_y}\le h(\eta_y)\le f(\eta_y)=-a,
\qquad h(n)\le-a.
\]
This bounds every competitor, including every noninvariant one.

For \(r\in|K^\times|\), \(0<r<1\), set \(c_r=a/(-\log r)>0\) and define the actual global function
\[
h_r=c_r\log\max(|x|,r).
\]
It equals \(-a\) on the entire y-branch. It is LFS on the singular space itself: on the ordinary neighbourhood \(|x|<r\) of the node it is constant, and elsewhere the logarithm-of-unit maximum presentation from n1 applies. Its bend lies at a value-group radius, so it is strict real PL. The ordinary-local presentations agree as a globally defined function; this is not merely a normalization construction. Also \(h_r\le f\): first-branch values are at most zero, and second-branch values satisfy \(-a\le-a|y|\).

At every nonnodal x-point, \(|x|>0\) and \(h_r\to0\) as \(r\to0\) in the value group. The constant \(-a\) is another competitor. These lower bounds and the full-family upper bounds compute
\[
E_Uf(z)=\begin{cases}
0,&z\in D_x\setminus\{n\},\\
-a,&z\in D_y\text{, including }n.
\end{cases}
\]
Each punctured branch is open away from the node and has constant raw envelope. Both accumulate at the node, using nonzero field elements tending to zero. Upper regularization therefore changes only the nodal value to zero and retains value \(-a\) on the punctured y-branch. It is discontinuous. The same calculation holds after every analytic scalar extension, since the branches, coordinate norms, minorants and maximum-principle bound persist literally.

By n2, for the pulled obstacle on \(U\times\mathbb P^{d,\mathrm{an}}\) the raw envelope is \(E_Uf\circ p\). Smooth openness of \(p\) gives
\[
\bigl(E_{U\times\mathbb P^d}(f\circ p)\bigr)^*=(E_Uf)^*\circ p.
\]
Its restriction along the analytic section through a fixed projective point is the nodal regularized envelope. Thus discontinuity persists in every positive-dimensional projective product. This excludes an unconditional continuity theorem for all reduced strict curves and their displayed products. It does not prove that every branched space fails, or that normality or geometric unibranchness is necessary in general.

Exact status: partial. The sufficient sectors in n1–n2 do not determine sharp necessary and sufficient hypotheses for original P03.3. Remaining gaps include arbitrary normal or geometrically unibranch higher-dimensional domains, the full perfected-unibranch curve range, general semistable affinoids and their global real-PL cofinality, arbitrary obstacles over nonalgebraically closed base fields, nonsplit singularities, codimension-two singularities, and general necessity. Compactness and projective-space factors are restrictions of the proved sector, not asserted sharp hypotheses.
